question: Given tables Employees(emp_id, name, dept_id) and Departments(dept_id, dept_name). Write a query to get employee names and their department names using INNER JOIN.
Write a query using LEFT JOIN to show all employees and their department names, including employees with no department assigned.
Given tables Orders(order_id, customer_id, amount) and Customers(customer_id, name). Show all customers and their orders. Include customers who have never placed an order.
What is the difference between INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN? Give an example of when each should be used.
Given tables Students(student_id, name) and Grades(student_id, subject, grade). Write a query to find students who have NO grades recorded.
Tables: Products(product_id, name, price) and OrderItems(order_id, product_id, quantity). Find the total quantity ordered for each product including products never ordered.
Write a self-join query on table Employees(emp_id, name, manager_id) to show each employee and their manager name.
Given tables A(id, val) and B(id, val). What is the result of CROSS JOIN? How many rows will be produced if A has 3 rows and B has 4 rows?
Tables: Customers(customer_id, name) and Orders(order_id, customer_id, amount). Write a query to find customers who placed orders with total amount greater than 1000.
Identify the error in this query: SELECT name, score FROM Students, Scores WHERE student_id = student_id;
What happens when you use a WHERE clause to filter NULL values after a LEFT JOIN? Explain with an example.
Tables: Books(book_id, title, author_id) and Authors(author_id, author_name). Write a query to show all books and their authors. If a book has no author, still show the book.
Write a query using FULL OUTER JOIN on tables LeftTable(id, val) and RightTable(id, val) to show all rows from both tables.
Identify the error: SELECT E.name, D.dept_name FROM Employees E LEFT JOIN Departments D ON E.dept_id = D.dept_id WHERE D.dept_name IS NOT NULL;
Tables: Enrollments(student_id, course_id) and Courses(course_id, course_name) and Students(student_id, name). Write a three-table JOIN to list each student and the courses they are enrolled in.
Explain why this query produces duplicate rows: SELECT C.name, O.amount FROM Customers C JOIN Orders O ON C.customer_id = O.customer_id;
Tables: Employees(emp_id, name, dept_id) and Departments(dept_id, dept_name, manager_id). Write a query to find departments that have NO employees.
What is the difference between ON and WHERE clause in a LEFT JOIN? Show an example where they produce different results.
Write a query to find pairs of employees in the same department using self-join on Employees(emp_id, name, dept_id).
Tables: Sales(sale_id, product_id, region_id, amount), Products(product_id, name), Regions(region_id, region_name). Write a query to show total sales amount per product per region.
Identify all errors in: SELECT * FROM Orders O INNER JOIN Customers C ON O.id = C.id WHERE amount > 500 AND name IS NULL;
Tables: Projects(project_id, name) and Employees(emp_id, name, project_id). Some employees are not assigned to any project. Write a query to list all projects and count of employees (0 if none).
Explain the behavior of NATURAL JOIN and why it can be dangerous to use.
Tables: Students(student_id, name, class_id) and Classes(class_id, class_name, teacher_id) and Teachers(teacher_id, teacher_name). Write a 3-table JOIN to show each student, their class, and teacher.
Given a query with multiple LEFT JOINs producing unexpected NULLs, how would you debug and fix it? Describe the approach step by step.
Write a query to show products that have been ordered more than 5 times using JOIN and GROUP BY on Products(product_id, name) and OrderItems(order_id, product_id).
Tables: Accounts(account_id, user_id, balance) and Users(user_id, name, email). Find users whose total account balance exceeds 5000.
What is a Cartesian product? When does it occur in SQL and how do you avoid it?
Tables: Flights(flight_id, origin_id, destination_id) and Airports(airport_id, airport_name). Write a query using two JOINs on the same Airports table to show origin and destination names.
Explain the difference between LEFT JOIN and RIGHT JOIN. Can one always be rewritten as the other? Show an example.
Write a query to find employees who share the same job title using self-join on Employees(emp_id, name, job_title).
Tables: Categories(cat_id, cat_name) and Products(product_id, name, cat_id). Show categories with no products using LEFT JOIN.
Identify the error: SELECT P.name, C.cat_name FROM Products P RIGHT JOIN Categories C ON P.cat_id = C.cat_id WHERE P.name IS NOT NULL;
Tables: Suppliers(supplier_id, name) and Products(product_id, name, supplier_id, price). Find suppliers who supply products priced above 100 using JOIN and WHERE.
Write a query that uses both INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN in the same query across three tables: Orders, Customers, and Payments.
Explain what happens to NULL values during an INNER JOIN vs OUTER JOIN. Give a concrete example.
Tables: Teams(team_id, team_name) and Players(player_id, name, team_id). Find teams with more than 5 players using JOIN and GROUP BY HAVING.
What are table aliases and why are they important in JOIN queries? Give an example with and without aliases.
Tables: Inventory(item_id, warehouse_id, quantity) and Warehouses(warehouse_id, location). Show items with zero quantity in any warehouse using JOIN and WHERE.
Write a complete query using JOIN, GROUP BY, HAVING, and ORDER BY to find the top 3 customers by total order amount from Customers and Orders tables.
